messages:
maya: FYI canary for cobalt-q3-int8 is emitting more toolcall parse failures than usual — ~4.2% vs baseline 0.4% on the structured-output set. rolling it back now but wanted to surface.
kevin: any logs/examples?
maya: here's a failing model response we captured:```{
  "name": "update_ticket",
  "arguments": "{\"ticket_id\": 12345, 'status': \"triaged\"}"
}``` parser error: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes. looks like single quotes ended up inside the JSON string.
sophie: ugh classic mixed-quote issue after quantization introduces weird tokenization choices. are these from streaming or non-streaming runs?
maya: mostly non-streaming canary calls. we also saw a few outputs with trailing commas in arrays when the optional metadata field is omitted (e.g., `{"items": [1,2,], "metadata": null}`).
kevin: possible culprits: decode sampling (temp>0), tokenizer split changes with qparams, or a subtle byte-level detokenization bug in int8 path. what's canary config?
maya: canary uses default decode: temp=0.2, top_p=0.95, max_new_tokens=60, k=0.
leo: quick mitigation: set temp=0.0 + deterministic beam/greedy for toolcall route, add a strict instruction layer telling model to use double quotes only. we did that for another model last month and it dropped parse fails to ~0.1%.
ci-bot: canary snapshot uploaded: https://ci.internal/canaries/cobalt-q3-int8/1809998888 — failure slices: optional-field-absent, mixed-quotes, trailing-comma.
sophie: long term we should add a post-processor repair pass (json-repair heuristics) but make sure it logs and increments a repair metric so we don't mask regressions. also add a lint step in the canary harness to reject single-quoted arguments.
kevin: I can spin a quick 1k request A/B: baseline vs temp=0.0 + stricter prompt. if that fixes it we can patch canary config.
maya: thanks — please also try toggling the tokenizer preprocessor: `--normalize-quotes True` and `--use-fast-tokenizer False` (we saw differences there).
leo: I'll open a tiny PR to the canary config with two variants and a repair-pass flag, assign to kevin to run.
kevin: running now — should have results in ~30m.
ci-bot: test run queued (#4821).
sophie: one extra ask: add a telemetry tag for which responses were repaired vs failed vs accepted. helps avoid silent degradation.
maya: agreed. putting a follow-up: if AB shows no perf hit, set temp=0.0 on toolcall route by default for all onboard canaries.
kevin: quick note — if we go temp=0 we might see more degenerate outputs (repeats), so we should keep the strict formatting instruction + repair pass as backup.
leo: noted. I'll add the telemetry + experiment matrix to the PR description.
maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: update: first 200 requests look promising, parse fails down to 0.6% on temp=0.0 variant. continuing.
sophie: nice. if that holds, let's roll the config change to the next canary wave and monitor repair vs fail ratio.
maya: closing for now — will reopen if anything spikes. :eyes:
